resources.string: Tap to see what your device can measure
Bluetooth sensors (thermometer, hygrometer, air quality), online weather, astronomy notifications and a digits-in-noise hearing test. They will only appear once they really work.
Good: conditions suit the measurement. Limited: the result is approximate or some conditions are not ideal. Unreliable: do not interpret the value.
Permission was denied. You can enable it in the app settings.
This device has no accelerometer, so this tool cannot work.
Heading from 0 to 360° with interference warning and optional true north.
finding your way on a hike

The magnetometer measures the Earth's magnetic field and the accelerometer tells which way is down; together they give the direction the top of the phone points to. When the phone is held upright, the direction of the back camera is used.

This is magnetic north. True north needs your location to compute the local magnetic declination with the built-in World Magnetic Model; without location, true north is never shown.

Metal, magnets, speakers and cars distort the reading. If the field strength is outside about 25–65 µT, a warning appears. Move the phone in a figure-8 to calibrate.
Surface and vertical (plumb) level in degrees, % or mm/m.
hanging a picture or levelling a shelf

The gravity sensor (or a filtered accelerometer) shows how the phone is tilted. Surface mode: lay the phone flat; the bubble moves toward the higher side. Vertical mode: stand the phone on its edge against a door frame or wall.\n\nCamera bumps and cases tilt the phone, so calibrate once on a surface you know is level. Quality is based on how steady the reading is over the last second.
Angle and slope, relative zero and A→B difference.
measuring a ramp or roof pitch

Shows the angle between the phone and the horizontal. Lay the phone on the surface to measure it. Use Zero to measure relative to a reference, or Set A and Set B to get the difference between two positions.\n\nSlope % = tan(angle) × 100. Steep angles close to 90° have no meaningful percentage.
Ambient light in lux from the hardware light sensor.
checking if a desk is bright enough for reading

Most phones have a small light sensor near the top of the screen. It reports illuminance in lux. Phone sensors are designed for screen brightness, so expect differences of 10–20 % compared to a calibrated lux meter.\n\nIf the value reaches the sensor\'s maximum range, the real light may be higher. Screen brightness is a different thing and is not measured here.
Live, average and peak sound level with 1 min, 5 min and 1 h graphs.
checking how noisy a room is

The microphone level is measured in dBFS (decibels relative to the microphone\'s maximum). This is not the same as dB SPL. To see an approximate dB SPL, calibrate once next to a reference sound level meter.\n\nPhone microphones are tuned for speech, so very quiet and very loud sounds are measured poorly. No frequency weighting (dBA) is applied. Audio is processed in memory only and never recorded.
Air pressure, barometric altitude and GPS altitude for comparison.
tracking altitude gain on a hike

The barometer measures air pressure. Altitude is estimated with the standard atmosphere formula, which assumes 1013.25 hPa at sea level. Real sea-level pressure changes with weather, so enter a known altitude to calibrate.\n\nGPS altitude is shown separately because it is measured differently: it can be less precise vertically, and on older Android versions it is relative to the WGS84 ellipsoid, not sea level.
Daily steps, goal ring, distance estimate and history.

Uses the phone\'s low-power step counter, which keeps counting in the background without the app running. Distance is estimated as steps × step length, where step length ≈ 0.415 × your height.\n\nIf there is no step sensor, a simpler accelerometer method counts steps only while the screen is open.
Speed, average, maximum, distance, time and ascent from GPS.
measuring a running or cycling route

GPS gives position, speed and accuracy about once per second. Fixes with poor accuracy are ignored, and small movements within the GPS uncertainty are not added to the distance.\n\nIndoors, between tall buildings or under trees accuracy drops. Recording happens only while this screen is open.
Field strength in µT and changes caused by magnets or iron nearby.
finding a hidden magnet or steel stud

Shows the magnetometer reading on three axes and the total field. Set a baseline, then move the phone: large changes mean a magnet or iron/steel object is close.\n\nThis is not a metal detector. Copper, aluminium, gold and most non-magnetic metals are not detected.
Length, area, volume, mass, speed, temperature, pressure, energy and power.
converting psi to bar for tyres
Converts between units using exact or internationally defined factors. Works offline and needs no sensors.
True north needs your approximate location to compute the magnetic declination.
Magnetic interference: move away from metal, magnets and electronics.
Calibrate: move the phone in a figure-8 a few times.
This device has no magnetometer, so a compass is not possible.
Lay the phone flat on the surface.
Stand the phone on its edge against the surface.
Camera bumps and cases can tilt the phone. Calibrate once on a surface you know is level.
This device has no ambient light sensor. A camera-based estimate is planned for a later phase and will be clearly labelled as an estimate.
The sensor is at its maximum range; the actual light may be higher.
The sensor is usually near the top of the screen. Do not cover it with your hand.
The microphone is used only while this screen is open. Audio is never recorded or saved.
Uncalibrated: shown in dBFS, relative to the microphone\'s maximum. This is not dB SPL and cannot be compared with noise limits.
Calibrated by you against a reference meter. Still not a certified sound level meter; no A-weighting is applied.
Place the phone next to a calibrated sound level meter with a steady sound. Enter the meter\'s reading in dB:
Too loud for the microphone (clipping); the value is unreliable.
The microphone could not be opened. Another app may be using it.
Can harm hearing with long exposure (85 dB and above)
This device has no barometer, so air pressure cannot be measured. GPS altitude is available below.
Air pressure changes with the weather, so barometric altitude can drift by tens of metres within hours. Recalibrate at a known altitude.
Above WGS84 ellipsoid (can differ from sea level by tens of metres)
Location is used only while this screen is open and is not saved.
Physical activity permission is needed to read the step sensor.
No step sensor: the accelerometer counts steps only while this screen is open (limited accuracy).
Daily totals are updated when the app reads the sensor. Open the app at least once a day for accurate daily splits.
Never use the phone while driving. Let a passenger operate it.
Low GPS accuracy. Move to an open area with a clear view of the sky.
Recording runs only while this screen is open; background tracking is off.
Earth\'s field is about 25–65 µT. Large changes indicate magnets or iron/steel nearby. This is not a metal detector: copper, aluminium and gold are not detected.
All sensors reported by the system (%1$d)
Ambient temperature and humidity sensors are rare in phones. Battery temperature is never shown as room temperature.
Delete all saved measurements? This cannot be undone.

All measurements are stored only on this device. Microphone audio and camera images are never saved. Location is used only by tools that need it and is not stored with measurements. No ads, no tracking.
Point the phone at the sky to see stars, constellations, planets and deep-sky objects.
finding out which bright star you are looking at

Positions are calculated on the phone from your location and the time: about 5,000 stars, 88 constellations, the Messier catalogue, the Sun, the Moon and the planets. No internet is needed.

In Follow phone mode the compass and motion sensors decide which part of the sky is shown, corrected from magnetic to true north. If the map seems shifted, calibrate the compass with a figure-8 and keep away from metal. Without these sensors, drag the map with your finger. Pinch to zoom; tap an object for details.

Planet positions are accurate to about 1 arcminute and the Moon to a few arcminutes, which is far better than you can see with the eye.
Planets, Moon, star clusters, nebulae, galaxies and meteor showers for tonight.

The app finds tonight\'s dark period from the Sun\'s position and checks which objects rise high enough, when they are best placed and in which direction. It suggests naked eye, binoculars or telescope from the object\'s brightness.\n\nIt cannot know the weather or how bright your local sky is; clouds and city lights can hide faint objects. Meteor shower peak dates shift by about a day each year.
Sunrise, sunset, twilight, golden and blue hour, Moon phase and moonrise.

Calculated from your location and date with standard astronomical formulas; accurate to about a minute. Sunrise and sunset refer to the upper edge of the Sun with normal atmospheric refraction. Golden hour is taken as the Sun between −4° and +6°, blue hour between −6° and −4°. Mountains and buildings on the horizon can change what you actually see.
Saved only on this device to calculate the sky. You can delete it in Settings.
Times are shown in this device\'s time zone.
Never look at the Sun through binoculars, a telescope or a camera viewfinder.
This device cannot detect where it points; drag the map instead.
Stays above the horizon all day.
Does not rise on this day.
A rough guide for a dark sky. In a city, start with binoculars even for bright objects.
Only nautical twilight tonight; faint objects will be hard to see.
Only civil twilight tonight; the sky stays fairly bright.
The sky does not get dark tonight at this location.
Too close to the Sun to observe safely
No bright deep-sky objects rise high enough tonight.
The Moon is %1$s%% lit and up tonight, so faint galaxies and nebulae will be hard to see.
Active now · peak around %1$s · up to about %2$d meteors per hour under ideal dark skies
Its radiant stays low from your location, so fewer meteors will be visible.
The app does not know the weather or your light pollution. Clouds and city lights can hide these objects.
Eclipses and satellite passes are not calculated in this version; check a reliable source such as NASA or your national observatory.
The Sun does not set on this day.
The Sun does not rise on this day.
The camera is used only while this screen is open. Images are not stored unless you take a photo.
The camera could not be opened. Another app may be using it.
Measure distance, length, height difference and area in augmented reality.
measuring a table, a doorway or a room\'s floor area

ARCore tracks the camera's motion and recognises surfaces. Aim the circle at a point and add it; the app measures between the points in 3D. The live value shows the distance from the camera to the point under the circle.

Typical accuracy is a few centimetres per metre on well-lit, textured surfaces within about 3 m. Plain white walls, glass, shiny or dark surfaces and poor light make it worse. Quality is GOOD only on detected surfaces close to the phone.

Requires an ARCore-supported device with Google Play Services for AR.
Estimate the height of a tree or building and the distance to it from tilt angles.
estimating the height of a tree

Hold the phone at a known height (usually your eye level) and aim the crosshair first at the base of the object, then at its top. Using trigonometry, the base angle gives the distance and the top angle gives the height. If you know the distance, enter it instead of marking the base.\n\nThe ground between you and the object must be level. The app shows the possible range assuming ±0.5° angle error and ±5 cm height error. Results become unreliable when the base is almost at eye level (far away).
Measure an object in a photo by comparing it with an object of known size.
measuring a picture frame using a bank card

Place an object of known size (for example a bank card, 85.6 mm) next to what you want to measure, in the same plane. Take a photo straight on, mark both ends of the reference and of the target. The length follows from the ratio.\n\nThis only works when both objects are at the same distance and the camera faces them squarely. The result is always approximate.
Area and volume of rectangles, circles, triangles, walls, boxes, cylinders, spheres and cones.
how much paint or flooring a room needs
Enter dimensions in the unit you prefer. Results are exact for the values you type; the accuracy depends on how the dimensions were measured. Measurements from the camera tools are approximate.
Brighter camera view in the dark with exposure, gain and a green night view.
looking around a dark storage room

Uses the maximum exposure the camera allows, the phone\'s Night mode when available, and a digital brightness boost on the screen. More boost also means more noise.\n\nThis is not a thermal camera or an infrared night-vision device: it cannot see heat and it cannot see in complete darkness.
Test tones from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, sweeps, noise, a left/right test and a high-pitch hearing check.

Generates sound in real time: sine, square, triangle and sawtooth waves, white and pink noise, frequency sweeps and an alternating left/right test. The volume is in dB below full scale and starts low; the device volume also affects loudness.\n\nThe hearing range check plays a slowly rising tone; it is a fun self-check, not a hearing test, because speakers and headphones limit what you can hear.
This device does not support ARCore, so AR measuring is not available.
You can still use Height & Distance by Angle, Size with a Reference and the Area & Volume Calculator.
AR measuring needs Google Play Services for AR on this device.
Installation could not be started. Install Google Play Services for AR from the Play Store.
Move the phone slowly to detect surfaces.
Too dark for AR tracking. Add light.
Moving too fast. Move the phone more slowly.
Not enough detail. Aim at a surface with texture.
Aim the circle at a point and tap Add point. Add a second point to measure.
Hold the phone upright and level sideways for an accurate angle.
Usually your eye height minus about 10 cm. Measure it once for best results.
1. Aim the crosshair at the base and tap Base. 2. Aim at the top and tap Top.
The base is almost at eye level, so the distance estimate is very uncertain. Move closer or enter the distance.
Range assumes ±0.5° angle error and ±5 cm phone height error.
Only valid when the ground between you and the object is level.
Place an object of known size in the same plane as the target, take a photo straight on, then drag the blue markers to the reference and the yellow markers to the target.
Both objects must be at the same distance and the camera must face them squarely. Tilt and depth differences cause errors.
These values do not form a valid shape.
The result is exact for the values entered; its accuracy depends on how the dimensions were measured.
This is not a thermal or infrared night-vision camera. It brightens the normal camera image and cannot see in complete darkness or detect heat.
The phone\'s Night mode is active for this camera.
This phone does not offer a Night mode to apps; standard exposure is used.
Photos are saved as the camera captures them; the screen boost and green view are not applied.
The photo could not be saved.
Start with a low device volume. Loud or long tones, especially through headphones, can damage hearing.
High level: keep it short and turn the device volume down.
Playback stops automatically after 3 minutes and when you leave this screen.
The sound should alternate every second between the left and right side. If both sides play together, or the sides are swapped, check your headphones, cable or speaker settings.
Use headphones in a quiet room at a comfortable volume. The pitch rises slowly from 8 kHz; tap the button as soon as you can no longer hear it.

A fun self-check, not a hearing test: phone speakers and many headphones cannot reproduce very high frequencies, and the result depends on volume. The upper limit of hearing naturally falls with age. If you notice hearing problems, see an audiologist.
This device plays audio up to at most %1$s.
Human hearing is often quoted as 20 Hz–20 kHz, but real limits depend on the person, the speaker and the headphones.
Follows the hospital spirometry procedure with the microphone: start, duration, interruptions and repeatability.
practising the spirometry manoeuvre and tracking your blow over time

This test copies the procedure used for spirometry in hospitals (ATS/ERS 2019): breathe in fully, blow out as hard and fast as possible and keep going until no air is left, at least 3 times. The app checks the same quality rules as a spirometry technician: a fast start, no pauses or coughs, a long enough blow (6 s for adults, 3 s for children) and repeatable results.\n\nA phone microphone hears sound, not airflow. It cannot measure FEV1, FVC or PEF and cannot detect asthma or COPD. Use it to practise and to compare your own results over time, always holding the phone at the same distance.
Explains your blood tests, blood pressure, SpO₂, spirometry, audiogram and eye results using medical guidelines.
understanding a blood test report before a doctor\'s visit

Type in values from your own hospital or pharmacy results. The app compares them with the reference range printed on your report (preferred) or with typical adult values, applies the classification used by doctors (WHO, ESC/ESH 2023, ATS/ERS 2022, GOLD, ADA, KDIGO, ICD-11), explains what the test measures and tells you how soon to act.\n\nIt is an information tool, not a diagnosis. Your doctor interprets results together with your symptoms, history, medicines and other tests. Nothing is sent anywhere; results are saved only if you tap Save.

Information only, based on widely used adult guidelines. It does not replace your doctor, who knows your history and the laboratory\'s methods. Children, pregnancy and some diseases use different values.

If you have chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, weakness on one side, confusion or another sudden serious symptom, call emergency services (112 in Türkiye and Europe) regardless of any value shown here.
Outside the usual range or worth noting. Discuss it with your doctor at your next visit.
Clearly abnormal. Contact your doctor within the next few days.
Possibly dangerous. Seek medical care today; call emergency services if you feel unwell.
Reference range printed on your report (recommended, optional):
Categories: ADA (glucose, HbA1c), NCEP ATP III (cholesterol), KDIGO with CKD-EPI 2021 (kidney), Endocrine Society (vitamin D). Critical limits follow common laboratory practice.
The oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells. Low values mean anaemia, commonly from iron deficiency or blood loss.
Immune cells. They rise with infection or inflammation and can be low with some medicines or viral illness.
Cells that help blood clot. Very low values increase bleeding risk.
Blood sugar after at least 8 hours without food. A diabetes diagnosis needs a repeated abnormal test.
Average blood sugar over the last 2–3 months. Anaemia and some haemoglobin variants can affect it.
All cholesterol in the blood. Heart risk is judged together with LDL, HDL, age, blood pressure and smoking.
The cholesterol that builds up in arteries. Your personal target depends on your heart risk; it may be lower than shown.
The protective cholesterol that removes cholesterol from arteries. Higher is generally better.
Blood fats that rise after meals, with alcohol and with high blood sugar. Very high levels can inflame the pancreas.
A waste product cleared by the kidneys. With age and sex it is used to estimate kidney filtration (eGFR).
A liver enzyme. Mild rises are common with fatty liver, alcohol, medicines or recent exercise.
An enzyme from the liver and muscles. Hard exercise can raise it too.
The pituitary hormone that controls the thyroid. High TSH usually means an underactive thyroid, low TSH an overactive one.
The body\'s vitamin D store, made in the skin from sunlight and taken in from food or supplements.
A vitamin needed for nerves and blood cells. Low levels are more common in older adults, vegetarians and with some medicines such as metformin.
The body\'s iron store. It can be falsely normal or high during inflammation.
The main salt in blood. Abnormal levels affect the brain and are often related to fluids or medicines.
A salt essential for the heart rhythm. Both low and high values can be dangerous. A blood sample that sat too long can show a falsely high value.
A marker of inflammation or infection. It does not show where the inflammation is.
Diabetes range (ADA) – needs confirmation with a repeat test
Low HDL – a heart risk factor
Possibly too high – check supplement doses
Low iron stores – iron deficiency likely
Borderline low – your doctor may check further
G1–G2 is normal or mildly reduced; chronic kidney disease is only diagnosed if values stay low for 3 months or there are other signs of kidney damage. One measurement is not enough.
Sit quietly for 5 minutes, back supported, arm at heart level, no caffeine or smoking for 30 minutes. Take 2 readings 1 minute apart and use the average.
Isolated systolic hypertension: only the upper value is high, common with age.

Very high blood pressure. Rest for 5 minutes and measure again. If it stays this high, or you have chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, weakness, vision or speech problems, call emergency services.
Low pressure is usually harmless without symptoms. Seek care if you feel faint, dizzy or confused.
One reading cannot diagnose hypertension. With home measurements, an average of 135/85 or higher is considered high (ESH).
A resting heart rate of 50–100 beats per minute is considered normal for adults.
Outside the usual resting range of 50–100. Fit people can be lower. Repeat after resting; seek care if you feel dizzy, faint, breathless or have chest pain or palpitations.
If you have COPD or another lung disease, your doctor may give you a different target, often 88–92 %.
Finger oximeters are about ±2 % accurate and can read wrongly with cold hands, nail polish, movement or darker skin pigmentation. If you feel unwell, trust your symptoms.
Fill in what is printed on your report. z-scores or LLN give the most accurate interpretation (ATS/ERS 2022). FEV1/FVC can be a fraction or a percentage.
Obstructive pattern: air comes out more slowly than expected (seen in asthma and COPD)
Low FVC with normal ratio: a restrictive problem is possible; lung volume testing is needed to confirm
Obstruction with low FVC: may be severe obstruction or a mixed pattern; lung volumes are needed
GOLD airflow grade %1$d (if this is COPD, based on FEV1 %% predicted after inhaler)
No significant response to the inhaler.
Method: fixed ratio 0.70 because no LLN or z-score was entered. This can over-diagnose obstruction in older people.
Green zone (80–100 % of personal best): continue your usual plan.
Yellow zone (50–79 %): airways are narrowing. Follow your asthma action plan and contact your doctor.
Red zone (below 50 %): medical alert. Use your reliever and seek emergency care now.
Enter the air-conduction thresholds in dB HL from your audiogram. At least 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000 Hz are needed.
Complete or total hearing loss (95 dB or more)
Unilateral hearing loss: one ear hears normally, the other does not.
Asymmetric hearing: the ears differ by 15 dB or more. Doctors usually investigate this further.
Dip around 4 kHz with recovery at 8 kHz: a pattern often seen with noise exposure. Protect your ears from loud noise.
Sudden hearing loss in one ear (within 3 days) is an emergency: see an ENT doctor the same day, because early treatment matters.
Enter the value from your eye exam, as Snellen (6/12 → 12, 20/40 → 40), decimal (0.5) or logMAR (0.3). Use the result with your usual glasses.
The two eyes differ by 2 lines or more; an eye doctor should know about this.
Sudden vision loss, a curtain or shadow, new flashes and floaters, or eye pain with redness need urgent eye care the same day.
High myopia (−6.00 D or more): regular retina checks are recommended
Hyperopia (long-sightedness): near objects take more effort to focus
Astigmatism: the eye focuses differently in different directions (CYL value).
ADD: extra power for reading, usually due to age-related presbyopia.
A prescription describes your glasses, not the health of your eyes. Regular eye examinations also check pressure and the retina.
This is not spirometry. A phone cannot measure lung volumes (FEV1, FVC) and cannot detect asthma or COPD. Only a hospital spirometer can.

1. Sit upright, feet flat. 2. Hold the phone 15–20 cm in front of your mouth, always at the same distance. 3. When asked, breathe in as deeply as you can. 4. Blow out with one hard, fast blast and keep blowing until you are completely empty. 5. Rest at least 30 seconds between attempts. Stop if you feel dizzy.
The room is too noisy for an accurate test. Move somewhere quieter.
No blow detected. Blow harder towards the phone.
Slow start: blow out with a sudden, hard blast.
Too short: keep blowing until your lungs are completely empty.
Interrupted: avoid pausing, coughing or breathing in during the blow.
Too loud for the microphone: hold the phone a little farther away.
Good session: 3 acceptable and repeatable attempts, as required for spirometry.
Not yet complete: aim for 3 acceptable attempts that are close to each other.
8 attempts reached; stop for today, as in hospital testing.
Compare only with your own earlier results made the same way. A clear drop, or new breathlessness, cough or wheezing, is a reason to see a doctor for real spirometry.
Measures your pulse from the blood flow in your fingertip using the camera and flash.

With every heartbeat a little more blood enters your fingertip, which makes the camera image slightly darker. The app records this for 30 seconds (photoplethysmography, PPG) and finds the beat rhythm. If the signal is not clean enough, it shows no number.\n\nIt is not a medical device and does not detect rhythm disorders. It cannot measure blood values, oxygen or blood pressure.
Records movement and snoring overnight and estimates sleep time, efficiency and awakenings.
seeing how long and how restfully you really sleep

The phone lies on the mattress next to your pillow. The accelerometer counts movements each minute (like a wrist actigraph) and the microphone measures sound levels to find rhythmic snoring. No audio is recorded or stored.\n\nIt estimates time in bed, time to fall asleep, sleep time, sleep efficiency, awakenings and snoring, and compares them with recommended sleep duration. It cannot measure sleep stages, oxygen or breathing pauses; sleep apnoea can only be diagnosed with a sleep study (polysomnography).
Seismograph and vibration analysis (FFT), recent earthquakes from AFAD and USGS, and earthquake safety guidance.
checking a tremor you felt, or measuring machine vibration

The seismograph shows acceleration on three axes at the highest rate the sensor allows, with peak, RMS and the dominant frequency from a Fourier analysis.

The earthquake list downloads official data: AFAD for Türkiye and USGS worldwide. Only the source's public list is requested; your location never leaves the phone.

The phone is not an earthquake early warning system and cannot replace official alerts.

Not a medical device. Camera pulse readings are less accurate than a pulse oximeter or ECG, especially with movement, cold fingers or poor light. A phone cannot test your blood: use the Hospital Results Interpreter for blood test results.
1. Sit still for a minute and rest your hand on a table. 2. Cover the back camera AND the flash completely with your fingertip, pressing lightly. 3. Keep still and quiet for 30 seconds.
Cover the camera and flash with your fingertip
The signal was not clean enough, so no result is shown. Press more gently, keep completely still and try again.
Heart-rate variability from a camera is experimental and only meaningful when compared with your own earlier measurements at rest.
Blood tests (haemoglobin, sugar, cholesterol and more) need a blood sample in a laboratory. Enter those results in the Hospital Results Interpreter to have them explained.
This is not a sleep study. The phone estimates sleep from movement and sound only; it cannot measure sleep stages, oxygen levels or breathing pauses.
The microphone measures sound levels during the night to detect snoring. Audio is analysed on the phone and never recorded or saved.

1. Plug in the charger. 2. Place the phone face down on the mattress next to your pillow, not under it. 3. Turn on Do Not Disturb. 4. Tap Start before going to bed and Stop when you get up. Sleeping alone in the bed gives the most reliable result.
You can turn off the screen. A notification shows that recording is active.
Measuring movement and sound levels. No audio is saved.
This recording is shorter than 30 minutes, too short to analyse.
Blue: still (probably asleep) · Orange: movement · Red line: snoring
Recommended for your age: %1$s–%2$s hours (National Sleep Foundation, AASM)
Less sleep than recommended. Regular short sleep affects concentration, mood and health.
More sleep than usually recommended. If you still feel tired, mention it to your doctor.
Sleep efficiency below 85 %: much of the time in bed was spent awake.
Falling asleep took more than 30 minutes.
Frequent snoring (10 % of the night or more).
The room was noisy, which can disturb sleep.
No notable findings for this night.

Talk to a doctor about a sleep study if you snore loudly and someone notices breathing pauses, you wake up gasping or choking, or you are very sleepy during the day despite enough time in bed. Untreated sleep apnoea increases heart and accident risk.
Experimental. Results are only meaningful with the phone lying flat on a solid floor. Footsteps, doors and traffic also create vibrations. This is not an earthquake warning system.
Converted from peak acceleration with the Wald et al. (1999) relation. A phone is not a calibrated seismometer; official intensity comes from AFAD.
Frequencies up to half the sampling rate can be measured. Useful to compare machines or check whether a vibration changes, not for certified vibration measurement.
The data source could not be reached. Check your internet connection and try again.
Set an observing location in an astronomy tool to see distances. Your location is never sent anywhere.
Source: AFAD (Disaster and Emergency Management Authority), official data for Türkiye. Times are converted from Turkish time. Values may be revised after review.
Source: U.S. Geological Survey, worldwide data. Values may be revised after review.
During an earthquake: Drop, Cover, Hold On

• Drop to your hands and knees next to a sturdy piece of furniture.
• Cover your head and neck with your arms.
• Hold on until the shaking stops.
• Stay away from windows, shelves and objects that can fall. Do not use lifts or stairs while shaking.
• Outdoors: move to open ground away from buildings, trees and power lines. In a car: stop safely away from bridges and stay inside.

• Fix heavy furniture and shelves to the wall.
• Prepare an emergency bag: water, food, torch, whistle, power bank, first-aid kit, medicines, copies of documents.
• Learn your nearest assembly area (e-Devlet or AFAD) and agree on a meeting point with your family.
• Know how to turn off gas, water and electricity.

• Expect aftershocks.
• If you smell gas, do not use flames or switches; leave and report it.
• Leave damaged buildings and go to an assembly area.
• Use the phone for emergencies only; send short messages instead of calls. Emergency number: 112.
• Follow AFAD and official announcements.

Android has a built-in earthquake alert system. You can turn it on in your phone\'s settings (usually under Safety & emergency); the menu location depends on the device. This app does not issue warnings.
Hospital audiometry method (Hughson-Westlake) with headphones: thresholds per ear and frequency, and the difference between ears.
checking whether both ears hear equally well

The app uses the same procedure as an audiologist (ASHA / ISO 8253-1): pulsed tones per ear at 250 Hz–8 kHz, \"down 10 dB after a response, up 5 dB after none\", and a threshold confirmed on two ascending presentations. Silent catch trials and a retest at 1 kHz check reliability.\n\nPhones and headphones are not calibrated, so results are in dB below full scale (dBFS), not in dB HL, and cannot be graded like a hospital audiogram. The difference between your two ears, measured with the same headphones and volume, is meaningful: 15 dB or more is a reason to see an audiologist.
Visual acuity (ETDRS method, tumbling E), contrast sensitivity, colour vision and Amsler grid on a calibrated screen.
a quick eye check between visits to the eye doctor

Calibrate the screen once with a bank card so optotypes have the right physical size. Acuity uses the ETDRS method: 5 optotypes per line in 0.1 logMAR steps, each correct answer counts 0.02 logMAR. Contrast follows the Pelli–Robson method, colour vision uses plates generated from colour science along colour-blindness confusion lines, and the Amsler grid checks for distortion in central vision.\n\nScreens differ in brightness and colour, and viewing distance is estimated by you, so results are screening only. This test cannot measure your glasses prescription or eye pressure and does not replace an eye examination.
Screening only, not an audiogram. Results are in dBFS (relative to your phone and headphones), not dB HL. Use the same headphones and volume to compare results over time.

1. Sit in a quiet room. 2. Put on headphones (right side on the right ear). 3. Set the volume to 50 % and do not change it during the test. 4. Every time you hear a beep, even very faintly, tap the big button. Some beeps are deliberately silent. The test takes about 6–8 minutes.
Bluetooth headphones may adjust volume themselves; wired headphones give the most repeatable results.
Connect headphones. Each ear must be tested separately, which is not possible with the phone speaker.
Tap only when you hear a beep. It is normal not to hear the quietest ones.
O red: right ear · X blue: left ear · Higher on the chart = quieter sounds heard (better).
The ears differ by 15 dB or more at: %1$s. Doctors investigate asymmetric hearing; book an appointment with an audiologist or ENT doctor.
The result may not be reliable: answers at the repeated 1 kHz test differed by more than 10 dB, or you responded to several silent beeps. Repeat the test in a quieter place.
\"No response\" at 8 kHz in both ears is common because many headphones barely reproduce it.

Because the output is not calibrated, the app does not give a hearing-loss grade. If you have trouble following conversations, ringing in the ears or have been exposed to loud noise, a hospital audiogram gives the exact values (you can then interpret it in the Hospital Results Interpreter).
Screening only. Screens and lighting differ, so results are approximate. This does not replace an eye examination and cannot measure your glasses prescription or eye pressure.
Hold a bank or ID card (85.6 × 54 mm) against the screen and move the slider until the box is exactly the same width as the card.
Do this once per device. Without calibration, sizes are estimated from the screen\'s reported density, which is often inaccurate.

Choose the distance and the eye. Cover the other eye with your palm (do not press). Wear your usual glasses. An E appears; tap the arrow showing which way the open side points. If you cannot tell, tap \"I can\'t see it\".
At 3 m you cannot reach the phone: place it at eye height and ask someone to tap your answers.
The test stopped because the screen cannot draw smaller optotypes; your acuity may be better than shown. Use a longer distance.
Near acuity (40 cm). A value worse than 0.3 logMAR (about N8) can make reading small print difficult.
Intermediate acuity (1 m), as for screens and dashboards.
Based on the ETDRS method (0.02 logMAR per optotype). A single crowded optotype at a time is shown, which can give slightly better values than a full chart.
Hold the phone at 40 cm with your usual glasses. The E becomes fainter step by step; tap its direction. Guess if you are unsure.
Normal contrast sensitivity for adults (1.65 or higher).
Reduced contrast sensitivity (below 1.50). It can come from cataract, glaucoma, retina or uncorrected refraction.
Pelli–Robson method on a phone screen: 8-bit displays limit the faintest level and screen brightness affects the result.
Use normal daylight or bright room light and full screen brightness. Ten dotted circles follow; tap the number you see in each one, or \"No number\".
No sign of a colour vision deficiency on this screen.
Possible red–green colour vision deficiency (protan or deutan type).
Possible blue–yellow (tritan) difficulty. This is rare and can also come from eye disease; an eye examination is recommended.
Errors on both red–green and blue–yellow plates.
You missed a control plate that almost everyone can read, so this result is not valid. Check brightness and lighting and repeat.
The plates are generated from colour science (dichromatic confusion lines) and are not the Ishihara test. Screen colours vary; a formal test at an eye doctor confirms the type and degree.
Hold the phone at 30 cm with your reading glasses. Cover one eye and look only at the centre dot. Without moving your eye, notice whether all lines are straight and complete.
Some lines look wavy, bent or distorted
Some areas are missing, dark or blurry
I cannot see all four corners and edges of the grid
Distortion or missing areas can be a sign of macular disease. See an eye doctor soon; if it appeared suddenly, the same day.
The Amsler grid is a home monitoring tool recommended by eye doctors, especially for people with macular degeneration. Check each eye separately, about once a week.
